jurisdiction.venue: U.S. District Court for the Central District of California

headline: Promoters Accused of Selling $3.85 Million in Weimar Republic and Tsarist Bonds Settle With S.E.C. for $354,676
deck: Regulators alleged Billy and Christopher W. Abshier promised $250,000 advances and multimillion-dollar government redemptions on century-old German, Chinese, and Russian paper. Both settled without admitting the allegations.

score_provenance.rationale: Combined civil penalties of $354,676 equal just 9.2% of the more than $3.85 million allegedly raised from 85 investors, with no admission of the allegations and zero criminal custody.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: SEC final consent judgments order Billy and Christopher W. Abshier to pay $236,451 and $118,225 ($354,676 total, 9.2% of >$3.85M raised) without admitting allegations, with civil injunctions and zero prison time.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Selling $38,500 worth of defunct novelty paper bills by promising a secret Treasury cash-out window
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: State felony theft charges with restitution typically matching 100% of investor losses, not 9.2%

sources.title: SEC Obtains Final Consent Judgments as to Two Defendants Charged in Alleged Multimillion Dollar Fraudulent Scheme Involving the Sale of Historic Bonds (Litigation Release No. 26688)

interactive_art_spec.caption: A 1923 German Weimar Republic 10-billion-mark Reichsbanknote. The S.E.C. alleged Historic Asset Placement Services Global raised over $3.85 million pitching mythical government redemptions on Weimar-era and pre-revolutionary Chinese and Russian bonds.
